subject: physics
title: De Broglie and Wave-Particle Duality
welcome_lead: Give an electron a wavelength λ = h / p and watch it diffract through a crystal.
meta_desc: A-Level Quantum adventure on de Broglie waves and wave-particle duality.
final_note: Everything is both wave and particle — only the scale changes what dominates.

concepts.def: All particles show wave and particle traits.
Pattern when electrons scatter off a lattice.

walkthroughs.body_html: If light is both wave and particle, why not electrons? De Broglie proposed every particle has wavelength λ = h/p. Confirmed by electron diffraction.
Electrons fired at a thin metal foil produce diffraction rings, identical in form to X-ray patterns. Spacing depends on accelerating voltage, which sets p.
For a 1 kg ball at 1 m/s, λ ≈ 7 × 10⁻³⁴ m — far smaller than any aperture. Wave behaviour is invisible for everyday objects.

mcqs.q: Electron diffraction shows electrons behave as:
When does an electron behave as a wave?
options: Electrons are sometimes waves and sometimes particles depending on the temperature of the apparatus.
Photon energy depends on how fast the photon is moving relative to the source.
In experiments that probe wave properties (e.g. diffraction through a crystal); in particle-like experiments it behaves as a particle.
Electrons are always waves and only look like particles at low energy.

mcqs.q: What determines the de Broglie wavelength of a particle?
options: Its kinetic energy alone, with no dependence on mass.
Its momentum (lambda = h/p) — heavier or faster particles have shorter de Broglie wavelengths.
Photon energy depends on how fast the photon is moving relative to the source.

mcqs.q: What determines the energy of a single photon?
options: Photon energy depends on how fast the photon is moving relative to the source.
A brighter light has higher-energy photons because intensity makes each photon more energetic.
Its frequency (E = hf) — only frequency, not intensity.
